provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The mechanism is a lattice made of the lattice colour (palette[1]). Some of its cells were erased to background (palette[0]), and the task repaints those erased cells with palette[2]. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates and uses only these three palette constants.

How it finds the lattice:
- It takes the bounding box of all lattice-colour cells. The box's four border lines are the outer frame, so they are always filled.
- The generator adds at most one interior cut-line, either a full inner row or a full inner column, never adjacent to the frame.
- To find it, the program counts lattice-colour cells in the interior part of each inner row and each inner column. A real cut-line has many such cells. Non-cut-line rows can contain at most one, where they cross a perpendicular cut-line.
- It takes the row or column with the highest count and fills it, unless every count is zero.

Only background cells inside the chosen lines are recoloured; lattice cells never change.

D4 needs no special handling: rows and columns are treated symmetrically, so any rotation or reflection swaps their roles consistently.

I departed from the archived solver's 'more than half the cells are 1' rule on purpose. Under the generator's 25% erasure rate, a frame edge of 7 cells loses its majority about 7% of the time, so that rule would mislabel a sizeable fraction of fresh pairs. On the supplied fixtures, my criterion and the archived rule give identical results. I checked this by hand, not by running anything.
draft_notes.limitations:
- If every cell of a whole frame edge is erased, the bounding box shrinks and the result is wrong. This is extremely rare.
- If a cut-line keeps only one lattice cell, it cannot be told apart from a perpendicular cut-line. The tie is resolved toward a row in visible coordinates, which can be wrong in about 1% of cut-line scenes.
- A cut-line with all of its cells erased is undetectable. That case is an inherent ambiguity of the task.
- The fixtures do not contradict the rule. However, the archived majority rule is not uniformly valid on fresh generator output, which is why the rule here differs from it.
- No tests were run.
draft_notes.host_review: The saved mismatch has exactly one interior blue point at (5,8). Horizontal and vertical cutlines are both legal and produce different outputs. This is latent ambiguity, not grounds to choose a solver tie arbitrarily. Original fixture hashes and factory unchanged.
draft_notes.host_sampler_revision: Preserve frame size, position and sampled cut orientation. Resample only the 25%-erasure mask, bounded at256 attempts, until all four frame extrema remain visible and a present cut has at least two interior visible points. This excludes fully erased cuts and ambiguous single-point axes, without dropping cutlines or shrinking geometry. All supplied fixtures satisfy the same contract. Distribution is conditioned on identifiability, not uniform over old masks.
